text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 11:04 UTC - elevated TLS handshake failures to api.redwoodinference.com from multiple POPs. 1m error ratio 13%. Code=TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE. Auto-page on-call.

sre-cole: Ack. Seeing repeated TLS handshake alerts on edge (haproxy/ALB). Streaming websocket upgrades failing, short 502s for realtime routes. Marking SEV2. Starting timeline aggregation.

support-jen: CS queue filling; 16 tickets in last 12 minutes referencing 'handshake failed' and 'connection reset during TLS'. Several paying customers impacted. Flagging for targeted outreach.

eng-runtime-ryu: cert-rotator ran at ~11:00 UTC for api-prod. Rotator reported success but there are reports of 'no intermediate' on some edge nodes. Pulling rotator run and node apply logs.

netops-ina: I see a terraform apply at 10:52 UTC that intended to touch a staging TGW attachment, but the workspace var was incorrect and a peering change was pushed to prod TGW at 10:53. Route tables show a short window of flapping at 10:58 where traffic for some subnets went via provider-edge-B which uses an overlay with effective MTU 1420. Also a management ACL change at 10:55 tightened ICMP rules; looking at firewall logs now.

sre-cole: early hypotheses: (1) incomplete cert bundle on some edge nodes after rotation -> client cert validation fails; (2) path MTU/fragmentation on new route + ACL blocking ICMP PTB -> fragmented ClientHello dropped; (3) stale DNS cache means some resolvers hit old/smaller clusters -> mixed behavior. Collect PCAPs, openssl probes, ALB node cert checks.

eng-runtime-ryu: rotator snippet:
```
[11:00:06] cert-rotator: run=rot-330 generated cert serial=0xa11f... uploaded to edge nodes
[11:00:09] cert-rotator: apply edge-a status=200
[11:00:10] cert-rotator: apply edge-c status=500 - missing intermediate
[11:00:12] cert-rotator: completed with 1 node partial failure
```
Edge-c logs show 'no intermediate in chain' from 11:01-11:06.

netops-ina: tcpdump from an affected AZ (11:02) shows ClientHello ~1700 bytes split across two IP fragments. ICMP frag-needed messages are generated but firewall dropped them while the ACL was in effect (rule pushed at 10:55). Example pcap snippet below.

sre-cole: quick repro from a host in eu-west-1:
```
curl -v --resolve 'api.redwoodinference.com:443:10.8.4.22' https://api.redwoodinference.com/health
```
Before fixes: sometimes returns 'SSL: certificate verify failed' or 'alert handshake failure'.

netops-ina: pcap excerpt (11:02):
```
11:02:06.211 IP client > alb: seq 1:1461, len 1460
11:02:06.212 IP client > alb: seq 1461:3161, len 1700   # fragmented ClientHello
11:02:06.213 IP alb > client: ICMP frag-needed mtu 1420 (firewall logged DROP)
```
Kernel on ALB nodes reports 'fragment reassembly failed' and TLS stacks time out during handshake.

security-omar: I pushed the ACL tighten at 10:55 to lock down a management subnet for a scheduled maintenance. Looks like the rule scope was wider than planned and denied ICMP type 3 code 4. Rolling that ACL change back now.

eng-runtime-ryu: checking ALB nodes: edge-c has missing intermediate and occasional 'private key not found' during 11:00-11:05. edge-a and edge-b show full chain. I'm reapplying the full bundle to edge-c and will hold off on promoting the cert to active until validation passes.

dns-bot: passive DNS monitoring shows some resolvers still returning IPs for old-edge cluster due to long TTLs set earlier (3600s). Those old-edge nodes are a smaller fleet and didn't complete rotation; that increases surface area. We'll lower TTL and push SOA increment.

sre-cole: mitigation plan (executing):
1) security revert ACL to allow ICMP frag-needed (11:07 UTC) -> in progress.
2) netops rollback accidental TGW peering change to previous attachment (11:08 UTC) -> in progress.
3) netops apply MTU clamp 1400 on TGW attachment as a stop-gap (11:10 UTC) -> planned.
4) eng-runtime re-deploy full cert bundle to edge-c and verify with openssl (11:08-11:12 UTC) -> in progress.
5) dns lower TTL for api A records to 60s and push emergency SOA increment (11:11 UTC) -> in progress.

eng-runtime-ryu: re-uploaded full bundle to edge-c at 11:09; openssl `s_client -showcerts -connect` reports full chain. Not switching active listener until we see error graphs improve.

netops-ina: TGW route rollback completed at 11:12 UTC. Applied MTU clamp to 1400 at 11:13 UTC. New traces show no more fragments exceeding 1400.

support-jen: CS update: error rate dropped from 13% -> 2.2% by 11:20 UTC after mitigations. A small tail persists for clients behind stubborn DNS caches.

dns-bot: lowered TTL and SOA increment at 11:11; most resolvers updated within 2-3 minutes; some corporate resolvers still cached for up to 20 minutes.

sre-cole: evidence synthesis: PCAPs + kernel drop logs show fragmentation + missing ICMP PTB caused ClientHello to never be reassembled -> handshake failure. Cert-rotator partial failure on edge-c introduced a secondary failure mode (certificate chain incomplete) so clients hitting that node also saw certificate validation errors. TGW peering change introduced the lower-MTU path that caused fragmentation; ACL change blocked ICMP -> PMTU discovery failed.

security-omar: action: enforce ACL change runbook and approval workflow for ICMP-related rules; add a guardrail tool that prevents broad ICMP denies (owner: security-omar, due 48h).

netops-ina: action: add TGW PMTU health checks, default MTU clamp setting for new attachments (owner: netops-ina, due 72h), and enforce terraform workspace checks to avoid staging->prod drift (owner: netops-ina, due 24h).

eng-runtime-ryu: action: update cert-rotator to perform preflight openssl verify, cross-node bundle sync, and canary percent deploy (5% for 2m) before global swap (owner: eng-runtime-ryu, due 24h).

support-jen + cs-luca: action: prepare customer-facing RCA and targeted outreach to impacted accounts, include timeline and mitigations (owner: cs-luca/support-jen, due 8h).

sre-cole: provisional root cause: multi-factor outage: primary = accidental TGW peering change routed some prod traffic over a lower-MTU path; secondary = a management ACL that blocked ICMP PTB preventing PMTU discovery; tertiary = a partial cert-rotator failure leaving one edge node with an incomplete chain. Combined, these led to high TLS handshake failure rates. Timeline to include in RCA.

sre-cole: timeline (to paste into RCA doc):
10:52 UTC terraform apply (staging workspace misselected) -> 10:53 UTC TGW peering change accidentally applied to prod -> 10:55 UTC ACL tighten blocking ICMP PTB -> 11:00 UTC cert-rotator ran (partial failure on edge-c) -> 11:04 UTC alert triggers -> 11:08-11:13 UTC mitigations (ACL revert, TGW rollback, MTU clamp, cert re-sync, TTL sweep) -> 11:20 UTC error rate near baseline.

eng-runtime-ryu: logs/snippets for the RCA (pasted):
```
[11:00:09] cert-rotator: apply edge-c status=500 missing intermediate
[11:02:06] tcpdump: client -> alb frag1 len=1460 frag2 len=1700
[11:02:07] kernel: IPv4: drop_frag: reassembly failed
[11:05:01] alb[edge-c]: SSL: no intermediate in chain
```

netops-ina: pcap excerpt:
```
11:02:06.211 IP 198.51.100.55 > 10.8.4.22: seq 1:1461, len 1460
11:02:06.212 IP 198.51.100.55 > 10.8.4.22: seq 1461:3161, len 1700
11:02:06.213 IP 10.8.4.22 > 198.51.100.55: ICMP frag-needed mtu 1420 (dropped by ACL)
```

sre-cole: RCA owner assigned: sre-cole. Deliverable: full postmortem doc with timeline, PCAPs, rotator run logs, ACL diffs, TGW route diff, DNS traces, and action owners to be published in docs/incidents/ within 48h. Handoff: sre-cole -> netops-ina at 12:00 UTC for follow-up. Leaving elevated monitoring for 2h.

support-jen: publishing interim status to status.redwoodinference.com and coordinating CS outreach.

oncall-bridge: handoff recorded. Moving incident to post-incident phase at 11:30 UTC. Will reopen if error rates regress.
